review:
I say this as a hardcore fan of the franchise but my patience is wearing thin as the game's technical problems are slowly eroding any fun I got out of this game. The game is constantly crashing about every 1/2 an hour on average for me. The game might be playable in 4 - 6 months time but for now, it is definitely not worth playing.

Game mechanics are more or less classic AC. That's great if you enjoyed any of the previous instalments. However, because Ubisoft has decided to force Multiplayer on us. Here's what you are missing out on if you just want to play the game totally solo single-player and not participate in any co-op or any of the guild (called clubs ingame) content (which I must add, the club competitions are NOT EVEN RELEASED YET) You are completely locked out of the 5 star gear upgrades if you are a solo player meaning you will hit a glass ceiling in terms of gear. 

The Armor set in Unity that can be unlocked is basically a reskinned Altair's costume (Either a Pro or Con depending on your preference), however it is basically a skin and has no statistical advantages so it is pointless to pursue if you are not a fan of the looks. I should also mention that you need to collect about 12 seals to unlock the gear which means it will take a while to do as well.

The Parkour is great in this game and probably the best in the entire series so far however as usual, it has a lot of stickiness issues. I've basically bounced about on all 4 sides of a window for 30 seconds or so because the game just doesn't want to let me climb to the exact spot to climb into a building.

Level design is much better than the last few games. Now they give you a more open area and let you figure out which route you want to take to get your target which is pretty fun when you perfectly execute an assassination. However there are a few levels (or some spots used in assassin missions) where the layout and guard density can get pretty ridiculous. Overall though the level design is pretty good in Unity.

The Stealth detection mechanics are pretty spotty in this game. I have encountered issues where guards were alerted of my presence after I stealth killed another guard on another floor or issues where guards all across the restricted zone are alerted to me when I killed a guard and there were no other guards looking my way.

Combat is a lot more difficult compared to previous games (which again could be a pro or con depending on your preferences). No longer can you fight off 20 or so guards and win easily. All guards carry guns which can take out 1/2 to 3/4 of your HP if you stick around too long so you have to try not to stay in combat for too long. The Double Assassination mechanics seem to be pretty spotty too in my experience. Even with 2 enemies clearly highlighted for a double air assassination, I have found myself frequently seeing Arno only hit one target which causes me to aggro the 2nd guard and consequently every guard in the zone is alerted to me. 

The Story is pretty meh and doesn't really take advantage of the interesting setting of the French Revolution which is pretty unfortunate. You only seem to read about the events of the French Revolution behind the scenes through the ingame journals or dialogue but are not really involved in many of the big events. I can't think of a single character outside of Elise who is memorable or even has any kind of personality. Arno is okay but is a poor man's version of Ezio.

Ubisoft has also included chests that rely on you playing a Mobile App to be able to unlock. I decided to give it a try but uninstalled it 2 days after playing it after it reset my progress twice. Another broken component of ACU... There is also an AC Initiates web game which I'm not too sure what the point of it is as it is still half built at this point on the website and it has also reset my level earlier. To unlock the legacy skins like Altair's Armor, Ezio's armor, etc  you need a certain Initiate level before you can open the chest. (Seeing a pattern with Club Competitions, Companion App and Initiates? I'm not sure why Ubisoft is adding in all these extra things to the main game when they are all pretty much incomplete, unfinished and bug-ridden)

Frankly if Ubisoft couldn't get all this working, they should either have left them out of the game completely and made sure their main game is fully featured and actually works properly or delayed the game release.

Before anything else in Unity, do yourself a favour and set the spoken language to French. I guarantee you, there is [i]nothing[/i] more annoying than sitting through a conversation between French aristocrats at Versailles, performed in cockney English – it is just intolerable. Even if you don’t speak a word of French, set the language to French and enable subtitles. The game is [i]at least[/i] twice as immersive in French as it is in English.

Besides that, Unity is the game that could. It [i]could[/i] have been the best in the series. It [i]could[/i] have been a smooth experience. The technology is there. The visuals are there. The gameplay is there. The difficulty is, for the first time in this series, there. Unity takes place in an absolutely stunning rendition of revolutionary Paris. There are crowds shouting in the streets, burning furniture and books, there are people going about with heads on pikes after beheadings.  Guards are smarter and more lethal and for the first time in the series you may [i]actually die[/i] from combat with enemies. You can also move better, more precisely and actually go and land where you want to.

The Nostradamus enigmas are absolutely enjoyable and give a high feeling of reward once you solve them – if you resist the stupidity of looking them up on the internet. The same applies to the murder mysteries – absolutely enjoyable if you play them straight. The main storyline is solid and has a good pace, though it can’t compete with the likes of AC II or Black Flag.

So why isn’t this the best AC ever? Basically, there is too much extra content and too much online focus. Too many weapons. Too many outfits. Too many co-op missions that need to be grinded again and again to unlock the aforementioned too many items. There are too many pickpockets on the streets of Paris and you get too many prompts to chase them down. Mind you that I played version 1.5 where these things are milder than the original release. However, the fact that even after 5 patches there are still some npc’s floating in the air above their market stalls is simply unacceptable.

The Dead Kings add-on is ok but really – it adds nothing to your experience other than a grenade launcher and some more hours of mercilessly assassinating thugs.

All in all though – you simply have to play Unity – because for all it’s little annoyances it is still an absolutely visually stunning game, with great gameplay, interesting characters and set in an interesting setting. Just as long as you do it in French….

I'm a huge fan of the Assassin's Creed series. As a history nerd and a huge stealth genre fanboy, these games are always right up my alley.

Now I'll tell you why Assassin's Creed Unity is, flat out, one of the worst games I've played in years, and why it's absolutely unrecommendable to everybody who owns a gaming PC.

I want to start off by saying that I was absolutely hyped for this game. More hyped than any Assassin's Creed game since Assassin's Creed 2. I had watched a few gameplay videos that sold me due to the fact that the devs seemed to be going for the classic Assassin's Creed experience: An emphasis on stealthy gameplay, an intriguing historical period, and a stripped down approach to weapons and gadgets. It hearkened back to Assassin's Creed II, which is an amazing game and probably the best in the series, closely followed by Assassin's Creed Brotherhood and Black Flag. 

The first drawback is the one everybody already knows about: The game is nearly totally broken at this point. Bugs are everywhere, the game hard crashes quite often, and it runs like a dog even on the most beastly of rigs. For me in particular, the most damning graphical drawback was some kind of weird frame stutter that I would experience literally every 4 seconds without fail, even in menus. I'm not sure what's causing this, but the game is nearly unplayable with it unless you're incredibly determined. As you can see, I have managed to bludgeon through several hours of the game, mostly due to its amazing recreation of Revolutionary Paris, which is by far the best aspect of the game. Most of that is wandering about the landscape and gathering collectables, which has been the peak of my enjoyment of the game, because any missions are so difficult to get through thanks to the fact that it's maybe the single most broken game I've played since Obsidian was forced to release Knights of the Old Republic II in it's half-finished state way back in 2004. And that's saying something, because that game was a broken mess.

There's been enough said about the games broken, poorly optimized state. I'd like to talk about why it would be a bad game even if it were to run beautifully. I'm going to talk about the past couple of AC games here, so bear with me.

I hated Assassin's Creed 3. Absolutely despised it. I thought it was terribly designed. It had muddy control and poor line-of-sight mechanics that often resulted in instant game over detections, it had awfully designed stealth sequences that forced you to follow people at ridiculously close lengths, and it had bad checkpoints that compounded both of those issues. A number of the missions (the midnight ride, the Charles Lee chase sequence) were just horribly designed to the point where they were frustrating. To top it off, the writing was utter trash, all of the characters were cardboard cutouts, and nothing was even worth following.

Then came Black Flag, which was a complete redemption for the series. The game was so much fun, it was beautiful to look at, and, most importantly for me, IT FIXED THE SERIES STEALTH AND GAMEPLAY DESIGN PROBLEMS! Control was smooth. Stealth sequences were designed well. Free running and climbing was nearly bug-free, quick, and intuitive. Trying to achieve 100% stealth in the plantation sequences were probably my favorite missions in the game. Playing Black Flag felt like the Assassin's Creed series had truly taken a step forward, like it was ready to get back to being the stellar franchise that Assassin's Creed II had promised it would be.

Enter Assassin's Creed Unity.

The reason I contrasted AC3 and Black Flag is because playing through Unity gave me the distinct feeling that I was playing a game designed by the AC3 team. It has the same exact pitfalls that I just described in AC3. Controls are muddy and you never truly feel totally in control of Arno. He lumbers to and fro in the vague direction you send him. A cover mechanic has been introduced that's way too sticky, way too close to guesswork, and generally hampers stealth so poorly that I completely stopped  using it except in sequences when the game forces you to. And, to top it off, they've redesigned free running and climbing with a system that seems like it should work beautifully, but fails miserably in every aspect of its execution. The days of your jumping off into odd directions, taking the wrong path up a building, and even inexplicably stopping in place and having to recenter the stick, then hit up again to continue moving HAVE ALL RETURNED FROM ASSASSIN'S CREED II. Seriously, bugs from a game that was made back in 2009 and were just solved last year have miraculously reappeared. How do you mess up that badly?

Add in that the music, something that was unbelievably atmospheric and really made the experience of Florence in Assassin's Creed II, and lent you sea shanties that stuck in your head for hours in Black Flag (and was utterly forgettable at best and terrible at worst in AC3) is absolutely unnoticeable. In fact, I didn't think about it once until, midway through this review, I remembered how much I loved Jesper Kyd's work in AC2. That's how forgettable it is.

There are also several instances of immersion-breaking content, including chests that are only open via the Unity Companion App, and microtransactions that are so hamfistedly jammed in they pull you right out of the experience. It's a basic example of an immersion murdering mechanic, and it boggles my mind that developers have not learned why you don't do these things in games. Hell, even the publisher and the money people should know why immersion is important for a single player gaming experience. There's no excuse for garbage like this.

You can also consider Ubi's utter failure to maintain some semblance of business ethics by setting their review embargo to 12:00 PM of release day, rather than the day of or the day before as is common practice. Why would they do this, you say? The only obvious reason that comes to mind is that they knew their game was an unfinished, broken piece of garbage, and they decided that their best course of action was to lie to their customers for as long as possible in order to prevent them from canceling their preorders. Despicable.

It really disappoints me to tear this game apart so viciously because I've been such a huge fan of the series. I'd like to believe that this was rushed out the door by Ubi, and that the team would eventually have produced a good game if they were given adequate time to have worked on the things that fail here. But at the end of the day, blame lies with the developer as well as the publisher.

"A delayed game is eventually good, a rushed one is forever bad"
- Shigeru Miyamoto

In conclusion, there is very little redeeming quality in this game. Unless you're an absolute history nerd or a super hardcore Assassin's Creed fan, this game is completely unrecommendable in its current state. Furthermore, even if the game were totally fixed, even if the graphical issues and the bugs were completely ironed out and the game ran beautifully, this still isn't worth a purchase because it's easily the worst Assassin's Creed and just not a great game period. The dev team here has an eternity of failure to look forward to, as people will forever think of this game as an exemplary pillar of Ubisoft's descent into the basement of video game development and business ethics. Hell, at least Watch Dogs had some interesting mechanics and some competent stealth sequences. This game brings absolutely nothing to the table. Just replay Black Flag instead. Or burn $60 in your backyard while punching yourself in the face, because that's a more valuable, entertaining experience than playing this game will ever be.

It's on sale. You're here. You think to yourself: "Should I get this?" You look for Steam reviews. Most people are positive but some are not. Then you see this review. This review is written by a madlad with more than 200 hours in this stupid game. This dude has spent more than in virtual Paris than he has in actual Paris during one of his holidays. He practically lives there. So you're curious what he has to say, so you start reading.

If this game is on sale and you're interested, get it. Just walking around can be fun. Get the no HUD mod from the nexus https://www.nexusmods.com/assassinscreedunity/mods/2 and immerse yourself in one of the best recreations of a historical city ever. 

If you want to actually play the game, here are my thoughts. 

Story is ok but not amazing. It has problems but whatever. It works for what it needs to do, which is give you excuses to do stuff in the world.

Gameplay on the other hand is great. Combat is slow but that's the point. This is mainly a stealth game. HUH, I hear you say, but yes, Arno can't just kill 600 soldiers in a few minutes, especially since enemies use the one thing he is allergic too a lot, namely bullets. A focus on stealth in an Assassin's Creed game, who would have thought. 

And the stealth is great (when it works). Sure, sometimes they see you through walls but that is the exception, not the norm. I highly recommend you watch this video by LeoK https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L5lB14UzX-U to get your stealth gameplay to an enjoyable level ASAP, because stealth has a learning curve and it can be frustrating, but once you can clear entire zones without being seen, you feel like a god. 

Parkour is great too but in my opinion it lacks a few moves, most notably the manual side eject. Still, it looks great and Paris is so dense that I 100% believe you can get anywhere from anywhere without touching the ground. Once you get in the flow it's amazing, and to get there quickly I recommend watching this video by Jcers for beginner and advanced movement techniques https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hnSQ-XQLWGE .

But now you are saying: "Yo, why the heck should I watch 40+ minutes of videos before I can enjoy this game?". Well, this game has depth. Unfortunately, it explains almost none of it. But once you start to apply these techniques your gameplay will improve because you improved, kinda like dark souls, and you just keep coming back. It's just fun to be able to show off in this game.

Multiplayer is also a thing. It's not entirely dead but not really alive either. If you click "play together now" the game will add you to random parties, which is your best bet for multiplayer action if you like me you have no friends. You can also try them solo, where they become probably the ultimate challenges.

Game is relatively bug free, but it still has some. It's still a Ubisoft and an AC game. Your mileage may vary, but I can't remember ever having a serious problem in at least 100 hours.

This is simply the best Assassin's Creed game on a mechanical level, and it is truly underappreciated for it. Give it a chance. I'll see you in another 200 hours.

EDIT: Okay, I want to add some things

The DLC is really great. Designed for after the main story, missions are challenging in both combat and navigation. The new area has a phenomenal atmosphere and the catacombs beneath are claustrophobic and sometimes even creepy. It deals with Arno's well being after the main story and gives him some much needed characterisation. Honestly the story here is better than in the main game. This is my favorite DLC of the old style of games.

I talked a bit about multiplayer but not about if it's good or not. In my opinion, it is, but of course if it works. There are more bugs and issues while online but it is still somethin I come back to. Missions are balanced around multiple players and playing with someone else and having each others back is just a great feeling. 

Finally I want to say that I play all AC games with a controller, except this one. If you play with a controller too and feel frustrated by the controls, consider giving KB+M a try. I remapped RUN to my right mouse and AIM to a side mouse button, and it feel natural to me. In my opinion, KB+M gives you more control, where a controller leaves you much more at the mercy of the game.

I don't think, that anyone in 2k23 really neads this review, but still. Here is my honest opinion on this undoutably ambitious, but sadly, an imperfect game. Let's start simple. The story.Well, to put in a few words, it's ok. There is no WOW-effect, especially concidering how janky it feels sometimes. There are missions, that follow each other, but the characters themself feel completely different. It looks like something inbetween is actualy missing. Other than that, the story is something you can actually enjoy for one play-through, but nothing remarkable. BUT, if you liked Arno, Elisabeth and others, you can check out a book by Oliver Bowden, "Assasin's creed: Unity". It is kinda stupid, that you need to read a book to understand the background of the story. But if you are searching for something to read - try it out. It won't leave you disappointed and is actually a good-writen one.Gameplay.Missions. Oh boi, i have to say a lot. Story missions are generally very well-designed. The assasination missions are the best in the entire series, in my opinion. The way you prepare to the assasination, the process, the planing, side quests - everything feels fun and interesting to play. Especially on you first (and usually the only) playthrough, when you are not that familiar with the game's mechanics. My advice - don't rush them, play smart and slow, it's much more rewarding. The other missions usually have some interesting gameplay evolved, but nothing to say about. You won't get bored, but also nothing WOW.The Murder Mysteries are cool. Unironicly cool. Aside from that - it's mostly garbage. Cafe Theater - nothing special, Helix rifts - SH*T gameplay-wise and are boring as fuck. Nostradamus Enigmas - cool, BUT I'M NOT WASTING MY ENTIRE F*CKING LIFE TO SOLVE THEM. Googled all, and STILL, it took me more than f*cking 3 Hours to complete them. But, I mean, the outfit you are rewarded with is cool, so I guess it's worth it. I want to complete this game 100%, so I have to deal with all this, and it's mostly just "complete and forget" type of stuff.Co-op missions and heists are cool.Open-world. Just superb, Paris is REALLY well-represented. It's insane how many NPC's out there on the streets, they make everything so much more alive. Yes, they are some-what buggy and sometimes feel unrealisic and kinda junky, but overall, really cool. The map design is also  very interesting. Unlike in 1st titles where you could spot the "Parkour routes" with ease, Unity has, i'd call it, a seamless map, where everything seems really realistic. One of the reasons I dislike the first games, is that the cities look pre-made and unflowy to move around, "the enviroment is allready there for you", if you want to climb this building - use these crates, these wooden planks that make no real sence for them to be placed between rooftops and so on. Of course, Unity still uses the same formula of moving the player around, but this time it doesn't feel like ther is a "correct" route to use. The amount of detales out there are also impressive, and they tend to blend out all those stuff, that are there to help you to move around. Parkour. It's beautiful. The best one in the series. I don't care if it's unreaslistic, too buggy sometimes. It is the one AND ONLY AC game, that you can boot up ONLY to go for a parcour session. At least for me. The general flow is insane. The way you move around, the ANIMATIONS, the city - it feels like you are the part of it. Everything is there for you, you need to only run and enjoy. But yea, this is the most contraviesial part of the game. Due to AC Unity's poor release, people tended to remember this gameplay as a buggy, unreallistic kinda thing with bad animations and such. This parkour suits my personal preferences, but I completely understand someone, that will say that it's not that good. At this point you have to decide, wether you like the game's flow overall or not. It all comes down to personal preference. I want to just note, that this game has arguably the most complex parcour system there is. The amount of stuff you can do with it is actually insane, trust me.Combat system.It's great. It is complex, but not too complex to be boring or too in-depth. You have different types of weapons, each of them have there uniqe style and flow, some tricks and stuff. Overall, it's enjoyable, but stelth is way more fun. Last but not least - soundtrack. All I can say - I listen to some OST till this day. That says a lot.DLC is cool gameplay-wise, adding a new weapon and a unique looking map. The story is also very-very cool, It felt even better then the main one for me. This was my opinion. I know people, who say that it's a game with a garbage story with plastic charactrers, bad buggy gameplay and is overall unpleasant and unflowy. I can completely understand them and, though I enjoy the game, I can't say that it's perfect. But I highly suggest you to buy and play it.Don't have a good day. Have a great day.

This is my first bad review on Steam, and it's not because the game is bad. On the contrary, I enjoyed playing AC Unity. But the numerous issues I encountered trying to play the game prompted me to write this review.

So, after downloading the game, UPlay will download, and you need a Ubisoft Account to play it. Okay, I created an account and played as usual.

Then the next day, when I wanted to play it again, I was asked to log in again. Okay, I tried to log in but couldn't, and UPlay said something like "there was a problem blah blah." I tried to log in via the web, and I was asked to change my password because of suspicious activity. Okay, I changed my password, enabled 2FA, set this device to be remembered, and I was able to play the game.
The next day, when I wanted to play, I couldn't log in again. I had to change my password again because of "suspicious activity." Then I repeated this problem until UPlay told me my account was suspended.

This could actually be a really good game. A masterpiece, perhaps. But it's all buried in this mess that's discouraging people from buying/playing it. And I think every Ubisoft game requires users to log in to Uplay, so, I guess it's time to remove all Ubisoft games from my wishlist because I don't want to deal with this kind of thing anymore.

(No story spoilers) 

*I have to say this at the beginning since everyone treats Unity as the black sheep of the franchise: 

Playing this game in 2025 is amazing, and it barely has any bugs at all during my playtime. Its flawless and so good! Please give this game a chance!

**Also PLEASE play this game in FRENCH with english subtitles. You will thank me for this. Because f_ck is this a horrible dub in English with the british accents everywhere. Even the voice actors are lifeless. The French voices and accents are PERFECT. This is very crucial to enjoy the game.

...Now for the review: As of writing this, I'm pretty much done with the main story. I only have one more sequence left, but I decided to write the review NOW since my opinion is still FRESH from playing. Why? Because I intend on taking a little break from the game due to burnout and life, but wanted to give a solid and fair score for this game. But we have to talk about the STRUCTURE and NARRATIVE of this game because its all over the place. Its just a mess. Not necessarily the story, but how things are laid out.

My biggest issue with Unity is that all missions from side quests are open from the START and they take place during different times and years during the French Revolution, and you might encounter a lot of spoilers if you decide to just do side quests blindly without a guide! So do like me and google a chronological list (order) of when to start what mission. There is an excellent guide on reddit for this!

BUT because of this flaw in the narrative, I felt forced to do a lot of missions that interrupted the flow of the main story. I still have so much to do before doing the very last sequence, but I have to play it canon-wise and in chronological order because that's just who I am with games and history.

Unity does a lot so perfectly, but the narrative and story falls flat. To me, Unity would have been the best entry in the franchise if it weren't rushed to release. Arno, the main character, had so much potential with his wit, charm. Paris itself is so beautiful and densly packed that its the best open world (city) we have gotten in any AC game.

Actually lets talk about the open world of Unity a little: Paris is without a doubt the most beautiful city Ubisoft has created. Period. For real, Ubisoft really suprised me with how alive Paris feels in this game. And OMG THE NPCS! They actually look and behave like humans, and THE SHEER AMOUNT OF NPCS ON THE SCREEN is bloody amazing. How does this game even run smoothly with so many people packed on your screen!? NEVER HAVE I SEEN ANY OTHER VIDEO GAME have this many NPCS and I don't understand how they did it, and why its not in future AC games.

My next praise is the parkour and combat. The parkour in this game is the best hands down in the series. Its so fluid, flowy and fun to execute and do! Its the animations that makes the parkour here feel so damn good. Its a shame we only saw this kind of parkour in Unity and nowhere else... But I understand why, since Paris had so much architecture to play with.

The combat is on the hardest its ever been in the series, and I'm all about that! Its amazing to actually feel scared to enter combat, and think if its worthwhile to battle or run. Its very challenging until you get better armor and weapons, and even then you have to stay on your toes.

Unity is just... So damn good, but its a shame it was rushed in production. This could have been the best game for many of you, but it has its flaws, but even so, I think its my new favorite in the AC saga. I love the parkour, combat and Paris. Its a treat to experience. The story is good, but underdeveloped very quickly.

But overall, I gave this game a 8 croissants out of 10 bagguetes. If it weren't for the stupid side quests it would have gotten a perfect score. They should have been progress locked, same with the DLC.

This game is a wonderful addition to the AC saga and one of the last predecessors that has successfully maintained its identity unlike the newer ones. The gameplay is incredibly rich, offering various ways to complete missions and an unforgettable finale that sends chills down one's spine. Although there are some typical bugs with the Ubisoft launcher, overall, the game is worth playing.

I will now delve into the major aspects of the game, namely the scenario/story and the gameplay/mechanics:

Scenario: Unfortunately, the game falls short in terms of development in the events addressed, and the historical context is not fully exploited. The different parts of the scenario lack cohesion, leading to a patchwork storyline that lacks an overall view. The conclusion is clumsy, and the metahistory fails to advance. This is a real tragedy and a beautiful irony of fate when considering the fate of the game. While the writing is accurate, the quality of the story is poor. Events are often rushed, and some climaxes fail to have the expected effect due to the plot's failure to introduce and work with its main and secondary characters. Inconsistencies are also present (sequences 10 and 12). Furthermore, the historical anchoring is merely a pretext, as contrary to the trailers, the game fails to centralize around the RF.

Gameplay: The parkour system has been redesigned to offer more flexibility, and the combat system has been renewed and gained depth and credibility, while still maintaining the series' signature choreographic quality. The resulting difficulty encourages players to use stealth, which is better suited for an assassin. The possibilities of infiltration have been significantly increased. However, there are some shortcomings in the game. While the game has ambitious customization options for Arno, a new and impressive parkour system, and a combat system with a never-before-seen tactical dimension, it falls short in comparison to Origins' combat.

Assassin's Creed Unity, set in 1789 AD, brings players to the heart of Revolutionary Paris, capturing the chaos and fervor of one of history's most turbulent periods. The game attempts to innovate within the franchise by introducing cooperative gameplay and deeper character customization. While there are flashes of brilliance in its ambition, Unity struggles to balance its new features with its established formula. This entry marks a turning point in the series, but not always for the better.
The story follows Arno Dorian, a young man seeking redemption and justice after personal tragedy. His journey through the Assassin Brotherhood is set against the backdrop of a crumbling monarchy and civil unrest. While the setting is rich and the historical context intriguing, the narrative itself lacks the emotional depth and clarity found in earlier entries. Character development feels rushed, and key plot moments are often overshadowed by pacing issues and an uneven tone.
Gameplay in Unity introduces a revamped parkour system and more complex combat mechanics, which add a welcome layer of depth to exploration and encounters. However, a major flaw lies in the forced cooperative features that require multiplayer participation to unlock essential character skills. This design choice severely undermines solo play, as it artificially gates progress and customization. It feels more like a chore than an enriching part of the experience, leading to frustration rather than engagement.
Visually, Assassin's Creed Unity is often breathtaking. The reconstruction of 18th-century Paris is impressively detailed, with stunning architecture, dynamic crowds, and atmospheric lighting. The artistic direction is commendable, offering some of the most immersive environments in the series. Despite occasional technical hiccups, the game’s visual presentation remains one of its strongest assets.
Overall, Assassin's Creed Unity offers a compelling setting and refined mechanics, but its potential is marred by design decisions that hinder player freedom. The mandatory cooperative missions required to access all character skills feel intrusive and diminish the experience for those who prefer solo play. While the visuals and setting are top-tier, the narrative and gameplay are held back by structural missteps. Unity reaches for innovation but stumbles in execution, leaving a mixed impression.
Assassin's Creed Unity gets a 6/10.

Masterpiece. In my opinion, the pinnacle of Assassin's Creed formula. Everything from graphics / lighting, controls to grounded, fast-paced combat and smooth parkour navigation has a cinematic, poetic beauty to it. I grinded my way to Legend Rank, collected all chests and other collectables, did all Co-Op / Heist missions and every single side-quest in the game as well as purchased every piece of gear / equipment and upgraded it. True 100% completion. What a game! :) 

My only complaint... Why the f*ck didn't Ubisoft implement a Start New Game option (you know, like in, literally, every game out there!??) in the Main Menu if you want to restart the game and experience it from the beginning, start to finish? Or, additionally, NG+ would have been nice. Why do we have to manually delete our save file from our system if we want to replay the game, losing all progress as well as multiplayer rank? LOL! Stupid decision. I know we can "replay sequences" but that only applies to main missions... and that way, we miss out on the "in-between mission" cutscenes / pre-rendered cutscenes... And why can we only "Quit to Desktop" and not to Main Menu...??

Anyway... :) I've heard a lot of people say the stealth mechanics are broken / buggy, etc... that enemy AI is too smart / sensitive to player movement and noise, that sort of thing. To that, I have one thing to say: Get better at the game. Use everything you have. Enemy AI is much more realistic than in previous games and enemy rooftop snipers have insane range and detection abilities. You have smoke bombs, cherry "lure" bombs, poison gas, guns, the silent, badass Phantom Blade along with Berserk Darts, etc... if you use everything at your disposal, if you're patient like a true Assassin, you become unstoppable. Period. You can be quick, clean and surgical; nothing will stand in your way if you immerse yourself in the deadly beauty of an agile killing machine who has tools for every situation. It's the best AC experience, the moment you get used to the new formula, because Ubisoft had to design this game on a completely new, updated engine. And you feel it! :) Years later, this still holds up as a true next-gen experience, both for gameplay, animation and graphics. And the soundtrack nails the atmosphere. Seamlessly combining classic, authentic instruments with Assassin's Creed's iconic modern / sci-fi-like elements.

Let's start off with the Modern-Day plot. Abstergo Industries' "Phoenix Project". Its goal is to discover people with high concentrations of First Civilisation DNA such as Sages and to extract the DNA of these people. They also want to develop and enhance molecular cloning technologies, so as to use the First Civilisation DNA available in order to clone entire First Civilisation beings back to life! Crazy, right? Lots of cool lore in this one for the hardcore fans. In AC: Black Flag and Rogue, you were an Abstergo Entertainment employee unknowingly working for the Templars. In AC: Unity, it's the opposite, you are working for the Initiates, an Assassin branch. A hacker collective led by someone named Bishop.

"If Arno was present for this Sage's death, it might lead Abstergo straight to his body. Naturally, we'd like to find it first." - Bishop on exploring Arno's memories, 2014

"Bishop contacts a Helix user who had just completed the memories of a Templar knight in the service of Jacques de Molay, the last Grand Master of the Knights Templar. She explained to them that they were being manipulated by Abstergo to sift through memories, following which she asked them to experience an un-sequenced set of Arno Dorian's memories as an introduction to the Assassin and Templar war. Once the Initiate had completed the first sequence, Bishop offered them a chance to join the Assassins. Once the Initiate accepted, Bishop showed them footage of Abstergo's Phoenix Project, explaining that the Templars were searching for Sages both in the present and past to map the Precursor genome. As Arno had encountered a Sage at some point during his lifetime, Bishop was hoping to find the Sage's remains through Arno's memories. To accomplish this, Bishop supervised the Initiate's Helix sessions, keeping Abstergo from finding out what they were doing, as well as decrypting Abstergo's confidential data during the Initiate's forays into Helix rifts."

Step into the life of Arno Victor Dorian. A devilishly handsome, elegant, witty and charismatic lad, often getting himself into trouble such as cheating at card games, getting chased around town, but serious and no-nonsense when necessary. A "French Ezio", you could say. Starting as a young boy whose Assassin father gets assassinated at Versailles Palace by none other than AC: Rogue's Templar protagonist Shay Patrick Cormac. Beautiful way to tie the games together. Now an orphan, he gets adopted by François de la Serre, Grand Master of the French Templars, out of respect and pity. He raised Arno alongside his own daughter, Élise, who quickly becomes the love of his life... Wishing not to corrupt the memory of Arno's biological father and bring his pupil to the Templar Order, François kept his Templar involvement a secret from the young boy. Despite this, the Grand Master died some years later in mysterious circumstances, murdered during a coup d’état orchestrated by another Templar, for which Arno was framed. 

The game is called Unity because of two reasons, in my opinion. One, because of the time in which the game takes place. The Assassin and Templar leaders were finally coming to an understanding, so close to making peace... But it seems not all members of both groups agreed with their leaders' ideas, leading to betrayals from within. But also, because for a short while, it seems like your enemy is becoming your friend (Arno's girlfriend, Élise, raised as a Templar) 

Wracked with guilt and blaming himself, Arno sought out the Assassins after escaping prison, the Bastille (in what is the best classic-style Ubisoft intro to an Assassin's Creed game, in my opinion) and finding out about his origins, to find redemption, through discovering his adoptive father's murderer and the motivations leading to his death, as well as to help those suffering injustice during The French Revolution. Ultimately, it feels like Shakespeare's "Romeo and Juliet" tragic love story, but it's well executed. A nice change of pace from the typical Assassin's Creed revenge stories, but there are similarities, as expected.

You meet many important historical figures such as Maximilien Robespierre, Napoleon Bonaparte, Marquis de Sade, Théroigne de Méricourt, etc... and many more iconic, memorable characters through side-missions, referred to as Paris Stories in this game. They're sure to keep you busy while immersing yourself in the atmosphere of late 18th century France.

In Dead Kings DLC, which counts as a bonus, un-sequenced memory, we see a more mature, cynical Arno following the tragic events of the end game, who, by this point, has fully embraced the Assassin Brotherhood, also fully aware of the dangers and ironies of both Assassin and Templar ideologies, eventually rising to the rank of Master Assassin. 

To me, Arno's growth is excellent. He just needed an extra, let's say... "push", at the end of the game, to finally realise his full potential, unburdened by his past.

Again, Assassin's Creed Unity, to me, is a masterpiece. Way ahead of its time. I mean, things such as the crowd system are insane. There can be way, way over 100 NPCs on screen at once, which you can use to your advantage to socially blend, etc... A lot of buildings, for the first time in the franchise, have fully realised, seamless interiors with open windows that you can parkour through to lose your pursuers, that sort of thing! The previous games had similar features, but not to this extent! A true Assassin fantasy / simulator. Back when it launched, it was riddled with bugs, but now it's simply amazing.

One of the most beautiful games i've ever played. 
The Notre Dame de Paris at dusk.. 
the angry Frenchmen storming the Bastille... 
The sight of the Guillotine with its infamous flower crown with the words LIBERTY OR DEATH and the silent procession of nobles to the execution block.

Paris is alive in its dirty, sick and stunning glory - from the loud markets, to the Versailles ballrooms to the slums where the poor beg for a piece of bread. It's as real as the awful past can get. Also, +10 if you speak French because the background voiceover is very well done with authentic French accents mimicking the bustle and hustle of a big city.

Atmosphere is something this game does not lack.

But it is absolutely true that it could have been so much better. The French Revolution is an amazing setting for a game and they didn't exploit it enough - Arno is a boring character (though hot AF.. damn boy), the story gets confusing at times.  

The co-op gameplay is as fun as the main trailer makes it look like and there are enough players almost 5 years later online that you won't run out of people to join the missions with you.

I think it's a shame that Unity has that reputation of being the 'worst' Assassin Creed game because honestly?? I think it's [b]hella fun[/b].

[u]Pros:[/u]
- [b]Parkour:[/b] Coming from someone who has played most of the AC games, I can say without a doubt that Unity has one of the best, if not, [i]the[/i] best parkour. There are a lot of things to climb on in Unity, and the smooth and fluid parkour animations make you feel like a real assassin. I've lost count of the number of hours I've spent just free running on rooftops. 

- [b]Environment:[/b] Paris is amazing. You can enter almost all of the buildings, and the interiors have amazing detail. The streets of Paris are filled with quite a handful of NPCs - lots of talking, random events happening - which I think adds a lot to the whole French Revolution feel going on. 

- [b]Missions:[/b] I'm talking about the sandbox missions in particular (including co-op), which I love. Most buildings have multiple entrances, and depending on your playstyle/weapon equipped, there are multiple ways to approach each mission. 

- [b]Stealth:[/b] Stealth is actually pretty fun, considering how you can easily get overwhelmed in combat in the earlier parts of the game. You have the usual assassin tools at your disposal (smoke bombs, phantom & berserk blades etc) but you can't carry crazy amounts of them, which forces you to do a bit of strategizing. 

- [b]Character customization:[/b]You can customize each piece of your equipment (hood, trousers, gauntlet etc), all of which has a distinct design. You can also equip different types of weapons (rifles/spears/axes etc) which can help spice up your game experience if you're bored with the usual sword+gun combo. 


[u]Cons:[/u]
- [b]Story:[/b] Not exactly a con, per se. The story is [i]okay[/i], but I felt that it could have been better, some parts more fleshed out.

- [b]Lag:[/b] It can get a bit laggy at times, especially at areas with high NPC traffic

- [b]Ambient music:[/b] Kind of a small thing, but there is no ambient music when you're exploring the streets of Paris. It's replaced by the sounds of the crowd, which, considering how many NPCs there are walking about, can still get quite noisy. It is a shame though, because Unity has a pretty good soundtrack. 


[b]TLDR;[/b] The story isn't one of the best, but in terms of gameplay, Unity's pretty fun.

This review may be extremely late in the proverbial game but I figure that it would be useful to take a honest look at the title now that a good amount of time has passed, Ubisoft has had time to release fixes, and gamers have had time to upgrade to relatively recent hardware. 

  The first thing I want to talk about is the question that a lot of folks will ask when taking a glance at the store page during a sale. It is pretty standard to see folks asking something to the effect of "Is it fixed?" and to that, I will say that with the patches that Ubisoft released and the better hardware of today, it generally runs and plays smoothly. I have recently started replaying it and have been rather impressed by how well it runs and I have yet to encounter any serious bugs. I am sure that some gaming youtuber somewhere will cite some montage video of wierd NPC glitches or something but when you are actually playing the game (and not just watching aforementioned montage), those issues don't really impact the experience a whole lot. Besides, such things happen in too many (often well regarded) games for it to be a serious issue anyway.
 
 Does Unity still have issues? Yes. Are those issues going to hurt the experience? Probably not as much as you might think. 

 Now on to the game itself. 

  Unity was Ubisoft's attempt to refocus the franchise and kinda go "back to basics" (for lack of a better phrase). Like the original Assassin's Creed, Unity puts a lot of emphasis on the assassination aspect with the player character (Arno) doing the bidding of the Assassin leadership in revolutionary Paris. It is not as focused on the main character as the Ezio or Kenway titles and instead gives you some insight into the organizational structure of the Asssassins and their war with the Templars. 

  That "back to basics" approach also applies to the gameplay. After years of Ezio and Kenway titles where combat with huge groups of enemies is rather simple and only a matter of hitting the counter button and attacking at the right time, Unity makes the player more vulnerable and even smaller groups of enemies more powerful and dangerous. Combat feels a bit more "hands on" than it did in prior titles with counters only doing so much and retreat often being the smartest option when you get in a big fight. It is a refreshing change and one that I wish Ubisoft had kept going forward with. 
 
  Parkour also recieved something of a make-over. It still works roughly like it has in prior titles but in Unity, it feels a bit faster, a lot smoother, and easier to manage (the E button forcing your character to climb/jump down is a wonderful thing). Moving about the city is satisfying and seeing some slick animations only adds to the experience.
 
 The stealth mechanics are a big thing in Unity. Older AC titles (and ones that came after) played it a bit fast and loose with stealth with a streamlined (and generally rather good) system. Unity adds some very specific parts in the game that require you to put a bit more effort into it. You have to very deliberately sneak around with a crouch button and good use of corners and other obstacles to block line of sight. This is yet another aspect that sadly did not really get pushed forward into later titles when it really did add a good layer to missions. 
 
 There are some downsides. I think it is safe to say that while Arno is a likeable character, his story is not the best in the franchise. It is not bad and it is still entertaining but those who are expecting Ezio or Kenway are probably not going to get the larger than life character that they are hoping for. Arno's story is more focused on (like the original AC) his targets and the intrigue that connects everything together. I personally enjoy the story but I can also see that it is not as strong as it should have been.

  Another downside is the way Ubisoft did the map. The location and how that location is presented is fantastic but when you go into the map screen, you will be greeted by a MASSIVE amount of clutter from various icons, collectables, and the like. The presence of these collectables is not a big problem but they should have handled how they show up on the map a bit better. As it stands, it is actually rather difficult to even find your objective marker when it is buried by locations for chests, co-op missions, and other collectables. 

  While on the topic of the map, I am sad to say that the whole tower/viewpoint thing is in place and while I understand why Ubisoft really likes this system, I think that they should have scaled it back a whole heck of a lot. There are too many viewpoints to climb and it kinda hurts the pace of the game. 

  There is one last issue. The customization was a good idea in theory but it was handled poorly. At its core, the system allows the player to use money they find to purchase new weapons and clothing. Sadly, they also locked some things behind certain conditions that sometimes breaks the flow of the game. I can understand some higher level (and rather unique) weapons and clothing getting locked behind certain extra missions or challenges but Ubisoft opted to lock even some rather basic stuff. It is not that this stuff is hard to unlock but that doing so requires the player to do things (like co-op missions) that may not be all that fun on their own. 

  While on the topic of the clothing, I think that Ubisoft's art department should have put more focus on creating clothing better compliments the overall tone of the game. Arno's own gear fits really well as it looks rather functional and even blends in pretty well. Sadly, some of the other stuff takes too many steps away from that utilitarian look and seems to be more about indulging players who want loud, ostentatious outfits than maintaining a immersive experience. I get why they went this way but I still think it hurts the overall experience a bit. 

  Overall, I think that after some time, updates, and a new wave of hardware, AC: Unity is actually a rather solid Assassin's Creed experience. It is not perfect but it is not NEARLY the broken mess that you might believe based on the coverage it got early on. I would even say that as a AC title, it ranks pretty high simply because it plays so well. It has a lot of little mechanical changes that really worked and were sadly abandoned in favor of what we got with Syndicate. 

  If you are a AC fan (even a casual one) who is thinking about getting this game, I think it is a safe bet to do so nowadays.

Assassin's Creed Unity is one of the best open-world action game ever.
-
A bold statement, but I really do believe it.
AC Unity is a rough game. Since its release, the game has been clunky, glitchy, and buggy - ruining many moments in your gameplay.
-
Despite that, AC Unity has a lot more to offer the player, more than its negatives, if you stick around and explore the mechanics of Unity. But firstly, let's talk theme.
AC Unity's theme is hands down one of the best and most appropriate for an AC game ever. The French revolution set during the transition of technology in warfare, the more use of rifles, guns and cannons, paired with still-relevant viable use of swords and melee weapons is the perfect recipe for AC game's combat, as it emphasizes the deadliness of an assassin as a rogue warrior utilizing speed and evasion.
-
And the words I used weren't just for dramatic effect, Unity is a brutal game, the player needs to gain or make the advantage by themselves in order to take on their enemies. A simple grunt in Unity may not be a threat, but 3 or 4 of them might, paired with the removal of counter-kill, human shield, and tick skin of the older Assassin's Creed game, makes combat substantially more difficult in this game, therefore making stealth important and worthy.
-
However, stealth in Unity isn't like most other stealth games on the market. Unity's stealth relies on the 3 T's: Timing, Tools, and Traversing. Timing, you have to observe for any opportunities that might open up, patrol patterns, blind spots, and using that knowledge in a timely manner. Tools, there are several tools in Unity that server different purposes, use them to help you kill enemies or sneak pass them. And Traversing, a true assassin knows how to use his movement and speed effectively. The parkour mechanic in Unity may be clunky and confusing at first, but try practicing with it for a while or may be look some tricks, and you can be the most stylish assassin, climbing and jumping from rooftop to rooftop elegantly like no other game can offer.
-
Overall AC Unity is the true Assassin's Creed experience in my opinion. The deadliness of guns and enemies make stealth a viable and worthwhile approach. The game becomes a lot more satisfying the longer you spend time with it and explore the possibilities. A really good singleplayer/coop game to sink your time into.

Assassin's Creed Unity is the last 'real' Assassin's Creed game. By that, I mean to say it is the last AC game that bared significant semblance to its predecessors. 

Unity is a controversial game among AC fans; detractors point out the disastrous release of the game, the lackluster story and boring world.

Fans, however, consider Unity to be the most refined of the AC games, with the best gameplay mechanics, breathtaking graphics, and incredibly fun implementation of multiplayer.

I fall into the 'fans' category. If there is one word to describe Unity, it's 'beautiful'. Among even newer AAA releases, I struggle to find games that look this good. AC Unity's portrayal of Paris is the most realistic video game representation of a city I've played; crowds of hundreds protesting and rioting the streets, hundreds (if not thousands) of enterable buildings including shops, coffee houses, apartments and palaces, each with bustling crowds of people inside, spontaneous crowd events such as thieves, gang attacks and general dickheadery. The developers of Unity really tried to recreate the Paris during the French Revolution as faithfully as they could. Graphically, both AC Origins and AC Odyssey fail to look as good as Unity (and note, all three were played with ultra settings).

Other than the world, other things I really enjoyed about Unity include the parkour and stealth mechanics, the multiplayer missions (which you can play by yourselves if you choose to - as this is an older game, there are less people online), the detective missions, and the combat system. The combat in Unity is difficult. Of all the AC games, I would say it is the most difficult. It is slower and more weighty than the others, but this all greatly adds to the realism of the game. Unlike in other AC games where mobs of 10 are easy challenges, I found myself often struggling when fighting more than three enemies.

All of these positives do not mean Unity is a perfect game, however. Despite its world being incredibly beautiful and realistic, critics of this game do have valid points. The story did feel rather rushed and simple, especially when compared to other games such as AC3. Other negatives I found with the game include that enemies with guns never miss, the Nostradamus missions at times were way too simple, and at other times way too difficult, and the over-cluttering of the in-game map. Additionally, while money in the game is not hard to come by, especially as the game progresses, I did find myself relying on spending a lot of time grinding ways to generate money in order to keep upgrading my gear and keeping disposable items (smoke bombs, bullets, etc) stocked. 

My main issue with Unity, however, is that despite making such an incredibly beautiful world, the game is poorly optimized. Like I said earlier, I played Unity, Origins and Odyssey all on ultra settings, and out of the three I got the least frame rates playing Unity. Also, as amazing as a crowd of 1,000+ people looks, there is a reason most games do not have crowds of NPCs that large; it is very demanding on your PC and GPU. I spent a lot of time watching NPCs rendering around me nonstop, and it is very, very noticeable and very, very annoying. 

Before I finish up the review, I want to quickly talk about bugs. Unfortunately, owing to its horrible release, bugs are what Unity is known for now. I am happy to say that in 2020, Unity is a bug-less game. While my game did crash twice, I actually did not encounter any noticeable bugs, visually or gameplay wise, so the developers definitely deserve credit for resolving everything this game had going wrong for it. 

In conclusion, I do think Unity is a great game. The only thing holding this game somewhat back is its story. Please note: the story missions are very fun, but the actual story feels rushed. Judging Unity on its gameplay and graphical and world-building achievements, I would have no issues saying that in these regards Unity is the best in the AC series. Were the story and initial release better flushed out, this would be considered one of the best AC games. As it stands to me, however, it is one of my favourites in the series.

Overall, this game feels like an Alpha release, and I cannot recommend this game whatsoever.

And also, the non existent "weapon wheel" is totally useless. ONLY way to get through weapons/gadgets now is 123456789 keys, no scroll, no button to hold to get the wheel up, which dissapointed me alot.

Whistle? Gone.
You cannot attract guards while in a hiding spot in any way now. You can only hope they will magically go to the haystack and "happens" to look into it for no reason.

Combat system drastically changed now, and I dont find it particuarly positive.
While going full on attack on a guard, another one can attack you from behind instead of the "what-now-waiting"
That is good.
But I still find the fights alot slower and boring to engage in now really.

Guards can no longer climb at all, so its VERY easy to get away from guards, way too easy really.

Now I have only written down bad things, because... I am that type of guy that complains alot, but its still all fact.
I know this is not really the kind of review people may want, but I really focus more on the little stuff that is bad with this game.
I also wrote all this meanwhile playing, so hence the un-formated sections.

Yes, the story is forgettable. Yes, Arno isn't exactly the most memorable Assassin in the series. Yes, the game launched as a complete disaster and you'll still spot the occasional bug years later.

But damn, Paris carries this game hard.

The city feels alive in a way few open-world games ever managed to replicate. Crowded streets, massive landmarks, incredible lighting and one of the best parkour system the franchise has ever had. Running across rooftops, slipping through windows and disappearing into crowds never gets old.

I didn't care much about the plot but I had an absolute blast just existing in this world. Ubisoft may have fumbled the launch, but underneath all that was one of the most immersive Assassin's Creed games ever made.

Flaws and all I'd still recommend it.

Reaction to this game has been laughable. I guess most people need to brush up on their French history and world history for that matter. First off, I find it silly that I have to explain that the world wasn't in 1080p until 1962, but that must be before your time. Open a history book! Do more traveling! This is Ubisoft's finest work yet and I am glad to have had the opportunity to play it this soon before the actual release in 2017. The game is pretty far along for being this early in the development process.

AC Unity excels in a lot of cases but has a few important weak points. This game has the best combat & parkour out of the whole franchise but the story leaves more to be desired. For a game set during the momentous event of the French Revolution it should have more involvement in the story.

It's still buggy, though nowhere near as before. The story's still meh, and online's a pain. But these are tolerable imo in exchange for what's not only the finest Assassin's Creed pre-Origins, but perhaps the finest open-world game of its time. Paris is still the gold standard of open worlds sans Breath of the Wild, and the parkour system is the freest its ever been, with plenty of hidden techniques to learn. Couple that w/ the series finally having a sense of difficulty and a much deeper combat system than anything before or after, and what you get is a redeemed, underrated masterpiece.

Assassin’s Creed Unity is a paradox:
As a historical stage, it’s unmatched a love letter to Paris that rewards slow exploration.
As a game, it’s a mix of brilliance and bloat moments of pure assassination artistry tangled in franchise repetition.

If you play it now, patched and polished, you’ll find a flawed masterpiece one that dared to push crowd simulation, architectural fidelity, and mission design into new territory, even if it stumbled on the cobblestones.

A game to savor for its set pieces, atmosphere, and assassination design, best enjoyed like a fine wine slowly, and with appreciation for the craft

At launch, this game was a mess. There is no argument in that at all. But now? The game is extremely fun, and a blast to play. 

The graphics are amazingly well done, all the way down to the small things in the streets to the fabric and clothes. Rarely I run into an instance of odd cloth physics or a out of place animation on character interactions. but other than that..from textures to the godrays..make the city beautiful.

The gameplay is amazing and not a button mash-fest like some in the series, meaning your attacks actually have 'weight' and an 'umph' when doing actions, this of course makes you take your time and sort of plan what to do depending on your enemy and the class that they are. Not saying its a bad thing to button mash, but I feel its more engaging this way and makes combat more enjoyable to me than "mash button until the enemy dies".

The sounds and effects of the city are actually really well done when you stop and pay attention to every little thing going on around you. The sound of footsteps changing depending on the terrain, the chattering of the locals, the fabric creating noises depending on if your wearing leather, cloth, or chainmail...its very impressive when you think about everything that is happening.

All in all the above makes this an awesome addition to the franchise. Even with its flaws such as..well, Coop is all but dead due to its really poor release state which turned a lot of people away from the title. The ones that I can connect to are in other parts of the world so connections are shotty sometimes. Even on PS4 I have issues finding people to play with in my own country due mainly that same reason.

As it is now I recommend this title, as it;

- offers an excellent story, with some cliche moments but still interesting to learn about in my opinion
- very well done controls on both KB & Mouse as well as using a gamepad
- the game mechanics work pretty well with only minor odd ball 'parkour' climbing animations but nothing game breaking
- the multiplayer is fun when you can find someone to play with
- The weapon veriety is a welcome change and really fun to play around with, to me anyway. It makes Arno feel like 'your' ideal assassin, from the animations, playstyles, and also the skills you choose to follow that all comes down to a different feel and experience that again makes multiplayer really shine.

I dont often write reviews but this game has come along way from where it once was, and yes probably too late to save it, but I will still recommend this game if anyone is looking into getting it.

I beat the game, and wrote a pretty popular review on Black Flag. I also work in QA, and love AC, and Ubisoft which I have a couple friends at.
That being said, I would like to explain in detail and reason, as to why I would not recommend this game.

Yes the game is filled with performance issues, that I would like to believe Ubisoft would be able to fix with time, at current the game is barely playable, it does not run at the framerate it should and staggers a lot on any graphical setting, plus has rendering issues.

But the main arguments is how different this game feels from the rest of the series.


Eagle Eye.

On Black Flag and previous titles, Eagle Eye worked as a Stealth Tool, you could not RUN while it was activated and it highlighted things for you for a short period of time.

This time, Eagle Eye can be activated while running, and even mid combat, how ever it has a Cooldown. Which is a bit off putting. Specially when the highlight colors for Eagle Eye on Unity is also the brightest shade of RED and YELLOW I have ever seen. It actually bothers having highlighted targets during Combat, which occasionaly it may occur.


Combat.

The Combat in AC Series used to kinda fit the series. Everyone in Assassin's Creed regardless of how nuts, powerful, skillful or influential is a human. Which means they can be killed by Blades and Daggers. So it was awesome and pretty iconic to stop a Super Villain's monologue mid sentence with Hidden Blades from Above. How ever now, there is even a QTE Fight against a guy, and the use of an Eden Artifact as an excuse to "Do it again three times" typical video game ness. Even Jobbers in Unity have way more health, and cannot be killed with a single Counter, which again made sense since it's a bunch of guards fighting an ASSASSIN, and you could up the challenge a bit by adding tons of guards that you had to time each counter to.
Assassin's Creed is a cinematic experience, I do not want to fight some random guards for precious minutes cause they somehow are able to Tank an Assassin.

Equipment.

Another thing about this game, you could always get different gear and stuff, some with stats too. But you never REQUIRED to upgrade your stuff. I beat most of Black Flag with default gear cause they looked neat, and felt part of the character. This time how ever it is a huge challenge to beat the game with default gear "Which I did, cause the rest looked ugly" since there's an RPG element to the game, where you have a "Level" for your character and each Jobber and missions too. And how ever you are able to play the missions they simply have more health, or you perhaps are not "As Stealthy" cause your "Stealth Stats" were not high enough.


Stealth.

And stealth also has it's issues, they made a lot of things look and feel different, even the Blending on groups of civs has a different type of visual to it, and is not as effective if you do not have enough "Stealth Stats" from your gear. Still works till the end of the game, but it's clearly dependent of these upgrades.


City.

The City is amazing, is the one part of this game that needs proper credit. The amount of NPCs on the screen is ridiculous. And gives the city an incredible detail and Life. The Revolution is displayed very well too.


Co Op.

I have not yet been able to try Co Op much since friends were not able to play or playing on PS4.
But as far as I see you have some neat options for creating your own Club, and having challenges, objectives. Form your own Creed. And meet other Assassins. There are a few options for different types of activities for your Co Op friends. And exploring the city with friends sounds amazing.

Story.

The story is pretty interesting, I don't see major flaws with it aside from not explaining the Eden Artifact used on this game AT ALL. Characters are pretty interesting, but they are barely used as to their extent.

Overall, there are a lot of glitches, lack of the Hidden Blade rendering during ingame cutscenes that shows the character stabbing a dude, even tents that have 100% visibility through it getting guards to detect you through it. Lot's of QA issues, and for what ever reason they decided to mess with a bunch of mechanics that already worked in the first place. Eagle Eye, Stealth, Combat. I feel like people bitched at how easy it was to fight in previous AC games and they tried to please those dudes, but Combat always made SENSE and it was cinematic.

I also believe this game might be pretty "Skipable", in terms of what it adds to the overall plot and the characters on it.

This game is old and was made almost 9 years ago, but I enjoy finishing it for two reasons. First, you experience the feeling of the old games of this series, which unfortunately is not present in the new games of this series.
The second is the good graphics of this game, which still after 9 years I prefer it to some new titles. The number of NPCs that are traveling in the city of Paris is so large that you will not see this number of NPCs in any other game. The lighting system of the game is wonderful and the motion captures are excellent and done with high quality. The rendering of the skin is outstanding considering that the game is a decade old.
Definitely, this game is not without flaws, but because it was released in bad conditions, it was not given enough attention.
What a pity that this potential was lost.

I have not played Syndicate or Origins yet so I will be writing this review without those in mind.  As a long time Assassin's Creed player I was wary about playing this as it obviously had mixed reviews and a rocky start.  And after a somewhat slow start, this game really picks up and has become one of my favorites.  

Pros:
-Great stealth
-Beautiful graphics
-They really nailed the history
-Really fun side missions (murder mysteries, puzzles)
-So many different ways to play (sneaky, brute, sniper)
-Action mechanics and assassinations moves change with the weapon and are super fun
-Brutal kills
-Above average story
-One of the best as far as attention to detail
-Changing weather
-Fighting was actually harder!  Gone are the days I can counter kill 30 people in a row

Now that being said there were definitely some things that could have been improved

Cons:
-Even with all the patches, the parkour was still a little "off", the animation is better and you can climb new corners and do new jumps, but the simplest things like getting off a table were a pain sometimes, but you get used to it
-Really miss some things you used to be able to do.  Like whistling people over, disarming people, picking up weapons, moving dead bodies, etc
-Most people have a british accent and it weirded me out
-Multiplayer was doable for one person but challenging, wish it was still working
-Can't get 100% completion without using their companion app and jumping through some hoops
-Story was good but could have been better (still no meaningful modern day)
-Starts slow and is a little overwhelming with all the history (but very detailed)

All in all, it was a great game and I think a big leap from the previous games.  It introduced a whole new feel and I think they just rushed it a little.  But the action and gameplay are amazing, you really feel like an assassin in this game.  If you like Assassin's Creed in general, you'll love it.  Get it on a sale and have some fun!

Assassin's Creed Unity feels like the last Assassin’s Creed game that truly understood the series identity. It focuses on parkour, stealth, dense city design, and grounded combat instead of trying to become a full RPG.

The graphics still look impressive even compared to newer entries. Paris feels detailed, alive, and immersive in a way few open world games manage. The parkour is one of the best in the franchise. It can feel difficult at first, but once the movement clicks, it flows naturally and looks incredible.

Combat feels clean, weighty, and dangerous enough to stay engaging. Stealth is also strong since enemies detect you quickly, forcing you to actually think about positioning and timing instead of rushing through encounters.

The story is decent but incomplete. Arno is a solid protagonist, but the French Revolution setting feels underused. The Dead Kings DLC improves the narrative a lot by focusing more on Arno’s personal journey, and honestly makes the overall story feel more complete.

The game had a rough launch, and a lot of the criticism back then was understandable. But today, the game is basically fixed. There are still some bugs here and there, mostly in co op. I encountered a few graphical glitches, clipping issues, and one moment where enemies spotted me through walls. None of it completely ruined the experience though.

What really makes Unity stand out is its replayability. The movement, stealth, and mission design make the game fun to revisit even after finishing the story. Free roaming through Paris never really gets old, and there are so many ways to approach missions that I keep coming back to it without getting bored.

Unity is not the best Assassin’s Creed game, but it is easily one of the strongest in the franchise. It feels focused, immersive, and confident in what it wants to be.
