It seems everyone hates this game, and they're not wrong. It's not a bad game, it's just substandard for AC. I only got to play this two years after it was made by which time the bugs seem to have been fixed, so I won't be complaining about the bugginess. Ubisoft seems to make these games on a schedule, and they're all very extensive games so it seems they publish them before they're finished, and fix the bugs over the next couple of years. As a general rule it seems like it's a better idea to play any AC game at least a year after it comes out.

By the time I'm writing this they've already made Syndicate and most of what I'm going to complain about here has already been fixed but I'm going to write this anyways for posterity.

Pros:

The city - Life-size, incredibly detailed, painting-like map of Paris.

The graphics - This is actually more of a con for me, I'm down for anything on par with and above Brotherhood's graphics, it's just when it's such a heavy game it compromises fps and playability even on above average gaming PCs. But the graphics are incredible if you can run them.

The combat system - I was led to believe from some of the reviews here that the combat would be slow and clunky, but I actually find this a lot more playable than AC's classic jumping around routine. Not to mention it's better than being zerg rushed by a horde of enemies who block your attacks and by the time you get to break the defense of one you're stabbed in the back by 10.

My favourite thing about this game is that you can equip a sword and the hidden blade at the same time, and Arno will use whatever the situation calls for. You can also equip guns and smoke bombs simultaneously.

The parkour - I mean, the parkour has always had its issues but this is quite alright, especially when compared to Syndicate. People seem to hate it but I can't understand why. Jumping sideways/down has some issues. 2 and Brotherhood were the high point, it made the puzzles actually playable.

The era - You can't really do much wrong with a French revolution game.

The helix rifts - I personally like them, it's like the developers tried to squeeze in as much of Paris' history as they could into the game. 

The sidequests - I normally HATE sidequests in AC games, every sidequest is the same, "follow that dude, find that guy in a crowd and assassinate him, can you outrun the timer?" but this game's sidequests have references to the edgier parts of Paris' history and they're not boring. 

The stage at Cafe Theatre where people do stuff.

Cons:

The characters - They're such painful cliches, there's the Jedi council talking Arno down for feeling guilt, Bellec's the grizzled drunken old instructor who calls his young apprentice "pisspot", Elise is a sassy Disney princess, Arno is completely unrelateable. We haven't had a likeable assassin since Ezio. Napoleon was surprisingly alright for a side character though.

The assassin order - They've changed every established recogniseable aspect of the franchise (by the time I'm writing this they've changed them back presumably because so many people were complaining.) The memory corridors don't exist, instead you relive your victim's memories for some inexplicable reason. The assassin initiation ritual with the pretend finger cutting is replaced by some kind of psychedelic wine that gives you express assassin training. 

The psychedelic wine - Psychedelic sequences in games are kind of a lazy way of making them look interesting without actually adding anything to the plot. All they are is platform jumping with weird oversized crap floating around, and warped checkerboard patterns. I found it jarring in this game, I had found it alright (if a bit too frequent) in the Arkham games because the situation actually called for it. Dream and psychedelic sequences are usually just uninspired lazy writing that got old after everyone started doing them.

The hacker cutscenes where you become an assassin by clicking "play" - I think Liberation must have been the game that killed the modern day stories. Instead of seeing how the past reflects on the present like you did in the earlier AC games, you get your game interrupted by grainy cutscenes from some preachy self-righteous hacker organisation. The modern day sequences in the old games were playable and they gave you the feeling that you were actually in the present, inside a machine. This just feels like a period game except every now and then the game stops for no reason and some uptight girl in a ponytail gives you a lecture. Syndicate tried to fix it by bringing back old characters but I don't think that fixed it.

The crowds - I understand that there would be crowds in the squares but aren't there any streets in Paris where one could walk freely without feeling violated? There isn't a square inch of personal space in this entire game, there's literally no room to stand except on a roof.

The plot - The game isn't actually about the French revolution, that's just the background stuff. The game is about Arno's love affair and murder mystery, and artifact hunting, and conflict with Bellec who has conflict with the Templar order, and meanwhile the French revolution is happening and the assassins aren't especially concerned with all that.

The multiplayer - It seems like they tried to make several multiplayer platforms for this game, except it ended up not becoming as popular as they'd hoped. Multiplayer would have been fun but it's poorly implemented and all over the place.

Microtransactions - Where you buy equipment upgrades and horse armour with real life money. I'm not opposed to paying for content dlcs, but this feels like a transparent attempt at ripping you off without giving much back.

The nomad/helix/creed points - The nomad points are from some kind of now defunct attempt at multiplayer, the helix points are a microtransactions money grub where you pay a lot of money for insanely overpowered equipment, creed points are like money but very specifically for equipment upgrades. Seems kind of messy and like they could find no other way of having people level their items up at the same pace as the game so they found a workaround by inventing a different currency for everything.

The XP system was bad in Syndicate, it sounds like Origins will be a grinding based World of Warcraft type RPG so I think they still don't quite have it down.

I've played every single Assassin's Creed game available and while this game is not the best, it's definitely not as bad as people say it is.

Highly Recommended.

This review is from someone who neither loves or hates Ubisoft games. I like to think it will be a very fair, unbiased review.


First and foremost, the game itself is awesome. The feeling of immersion I get from playing it is literally unmatched. Just walking around, I get the feeling that the NPC's are all real people with lives and things. You'll be running around and see people protesting at Notre Dame, people running away carrying items they looted, etc. The city looks both absolutely stunning and on the brink of chaos all at the same time. The free-running aspect has been much improved, but there are still instances where the game won't fully understand where I'm trying to point Arno and instead run him up a random lightpost mid chase. Assassination missions are completely open to however you want to go about it. You get heavily rewarded for utilizing the stealth aspect of the game, and not running into a situation guns blazing and sword swinging. I rate the game itself a 9/10.

But should you buy the game right now? Absolutely not. Unless you have a super high-end PC, you won't get above 30 FPS as it is now. I have a GTX 660, overclocked to 1385 MHz, 8 GBs of ram, and a Core i5 4670k, and even when I turn the game down to 720p and use FXAA anti-aliasing, the game doesn't seem to get much above 20-25 FPS. I watched a screen cap on youtube of a guy who claims to be running the game with 2 GTX 980's in SLI and he didn't get much above 45-50 FPS, and that's over $1,100 in graphics alone. I highly doubt this is something Ubisoft can fix with a simple patch considering I believe this is a problem within the core of the game itself. Not only that, it's incredibly inconsistent. Sometimes I'll load it up and it will play just fine, other times it will crash as soon as it starts having changed no settings whatsoever. Co-op is a nightmare right now. Not only is it horrible to try and connect to a game, but UPlay frequently is down.

TL;DR: The game is awesome. But don't buy it unless you have no friends who are interested in playing with you and a gaming optimized high-end PC.

I have played any of the Assassins Creed games in chronological order, so this review is based on the fact that I haven't made any experience with Syndicate, Chronicles, Origins and Oddysey. And another very important point for me is that I don't like to compare games with other ones.

The world of Assassins Creed Unity is big and we find ourselves in the Paris at the time of the french revolution. The character we play is Arno Dorian, at the beginning a young boy, who knows nothing about the hundreds of years old conflict  between the Assassins and the Templars. After a fatefull happening he meets his following mentor, Pierre Bellec, an Assassin, and gets initiated into the Brotherhood of the Assassins and reveals a conspiracy, by trying to discover to what happenend in his earlier years with his father. There are some kind of similarities to the story to Assassins Creed II, but Arno has his own motivies and also his own developement during the whole story. Important and what this series makes up is the fact that you meet many historical persons, in that case for example Robespierre or Napoleon.

The setting of this games is as I mentioned earlier is Paris and Versailles at the time of the french revolution. Many details you can see walking through the streets there are much buildings you can walk into. Masses of people in the streets and places who are crying about the King and the bad circumstances they live in. The feeling that there is a revolution coming is totally overwhelming and realistic.

With the graphics I didn't had any issues, as many other reviews say something else. In over 146 hours playtime I had maybe two glitches when the body of a killed guard was flying through the street. I was always playing in the highest settings and had no framerate issues, even if I was walking through a crowd of 200 or more people. After Black Flag Ubisoft has improved again the graphics and details in Unity. Many little details we can see climbing on churches like gargoyles and waterspouts. Burning road blokades which gives you a better feeling for the revolution and many more.

What is way more difficult than in other Assassins Creed games is the combat system. It has changed that even a crowd of guards could be killed one by one, and anyone else was waiting. In Unity they pool together against you and also your enemies withstand more than in earlier parts of the series. At the beginning it might be a little bit frustrating and irritating but you can learn very fast how to handle with it.

Also improved has the free running and parkour system. It is now possible to make a controlled and rapid climb-down to get fast from the rooftops. Also you can slide under tables or swing through windows during you are running and chasing a marked person through buildings. Anything you do feels more smooth and has sometimes the look like the parcour guys nowadays.

What you also have is again a home base where you can ear money for buy buildings in whole Paris, also you get there a couple of sidequests. There is also a room for your robes and outfits you can find in chests. Besides that there are so many sidequests and little tasks you can do. the 3-D-map is full of it. Many chests with money, quests for the Assassins, collecting stuff, climbing the viewpoints of each district, which help you to get faster from one point to another and many many more.

The character customization is more extensive than before. The variety of swords, heavy weapons, chest guards, belts, coats and for your legs is enormous. There are also some kind of perks you can by with a special in-game-currency, but I have never done that because it's not important, and you have to spend real money for that. 

A new feature is that Unity gives you the opportunity to play coop missions. You can join some kind of guild or brotherhood which exists already of found one on your own. You can play those missions with your guild members or if there is no one online you can search random players for those missions.

A feature that is implemented since Assassins Creed Brotherhood are the optional missions which you need to do to get 100% of the game. You always to have look during a mission what are those tasks because they are not shown on the HUD.

At least the story of Assassins Creed Unity has been extended with DLC Dead Kings. To do anything you will have to spent about 7 hours, if you like rush maybe less. But it's fine and you will have fun with it, because there are agains some little new features.

Pros:

- beautiful and detailed graphics
- very good story, many historic persons
- Paris as setting is awesome and full of life
- many sidequests and little things to do
- stealth is more important (I didn't mention that)
- combat system is more difficult
- home base
- coop missions
- character customization

AC Unity Is Great! - Detailed Review

For anyone taking the time to read this, it's going to be a long review, as I want to cover the many reasons why I think AC: Unity is great, despite what a lot of other reviews say.  Note that I've just started (20 hrs) playing it in 2018, after finishing AC: Origins, Sydicate, and AC 2.

Technical: GTX960 4GB; i5-4700K; 8GB Ram.  I maintain 60 fps with textures and environment settings cranked, but AF on the mid-range setting and shadows on high (instead of ultra high).  My frames occasionally dip to 35 and typically stay 45-60, even with large crowds.  This game is NOT optimized, as I can't crank up typical graphics settings that I do in newer games like GR: Wildlands or even AC: Origins.  That being said, the game is gorgeous, and it's really unfortunate Ubisoft didn't take the time to optimize it.

Glitches: I haven't seen any of the reported ones from years ago, and very occasional pop-in.  Nothing has broken my immersion.

Comprisons:  When it comes to third-person, story-driven, open world games the following are at the top of my list: MGSV: Phantom Pain, Horizon: Zero Dawn, Unchartered 4, The Last of Us.  Each of those games did different things superbly but also each also had their flaws.  From an AC standpoint, I'm a long-time lover of the series, but have played a lot of AC games to completion in just the past 2 years.

I would hold AC 2 at the top of the Assassin's Creed list as one of the best over-all.  I liked Brotherhood and Revelations but they felt like more of the same and because I played them immediately after completing 2, so I think it was a case of Ezio-fatigue.  Black Flag was a great pirate game, and I loved certain aspects, but wasn't crazy about the naval focus, which puts me in the minority I think.  I recently completed Origins and loved many aspects of it, but found it to be a significant departure (good in some ways, not great in others).  I've never played 3 and put a bunch of hours into Syndicate before finally trying Unity.

Review:  I am so sad I waited this long to get into this game.  There are so many bad reviews out there and this game typically hits the bottom of "ranked" lists.  Noting what I've said above (self-fatigue especially), I would rank this game below AC2 (barely), but easily on par with Brotherhood (from a gameplay perspective) and above Origins, Revelations, Black Flag, and Syndicate.  Unity is the most polished gameplay, combat, environment, and framework of AC before all the big changes in Origins.  Here's why:

The story - it's a tried-and-true story very similar to the Ezio series: spoiled kid loses loved one, grows into a spoiled brash young adult, matures through circumstance, becomes assassin, is driven by revenge, etc.  Here's the thing: the DELIVERY of this story is very good.  The story isn't the best ever, but the delivery is very similar to AC2, which I love.  It lets you get to know and sympathize with the character, while learning game systems and getting well-paced story pieces to drive you forward into the world.  Compared to, say, AC: Origins, it's better.  AC: Origins has, at least, an on-par story but the DELIVERY is horrible.  Without spoiling, if they had introduced us to Bayek as a young father, and taken us through some events chronologically, I would have had a vastly-improved first half of the game, and been able to really step into the shoes of the main character.  

The setting - if you are an AC2 fan, this should more than satisfy you.  It's a different time period of course, but similar city tropes to navigate and wow is it full.  This is a detailed game.  Yes, the lack of graphical optimization ocassionally hurts, but it's easy to overlook.  There is SO much going on, and the ability to transition in and out of buildings is a great addition.  Which brings me to...

The graphics - wow, this game is beautiful, and, unfortunately not optimized.  It's hard to believe, but I would say it's very close to the quality of 2017 games.  The problem is that I can't crank up all of the graphical bells and whistles without suffering some frame rate issues.  As I stated above, I'm running at a tweaked "High" setting and it still looks incredible.  

The combat - this is the most polished AC combat pre-Origins, and yes, way better than Syndicate. I loved the satisfying combat of the early AC games but quickly grew tired of the "enemies wait" mechanic.  In Unity the enemies can gang up on you but don't "wait their turn" so combat is much more difficult.  It encourages a stealthy approach which I love, but combat can be mastered, it looks deadly, and is tons of fun.  

The free-running/parkour -  so good, second only to Origins.  You may "dance" on a window ledge from time to time only because the game gives you so many options sometimes you have to stop and think (gasp).  From rooftops to city streets to swinging into open windows this is the best it's ever been in a dense city setting. 

Other bits - the "home base" mechanic is one I love and Unity gets extremely close (if not better) than AC 2.  There is a room for everything in addition to secret passages, hidden armour, and a lot more.

The money making also feels very similar to AC2 in that it feels like an uphill battle at first but if you focus on building up your base the money will come rolling in very quickly.

The character customization is the best it's been and better than Syndicate by far.  They need to bring this level of flexibility back for future games.  

Lastly, the map.  I'm torn on this one.  It's a great map that transitions from topographical to 3-D seamlessly but the management of icons can feel cluttered. 

Conclusion: this is an ironic game of polish - the aging systems have never felt so good, and if Ubisoft had only polished the game itself it wouldn't have drowned in glitches and angry gamers at release.  There are many moments that made me cheer, and if you're looking to live out action sequences as a musketeer, with a dash of Count of Monte Cristo, this game delivers on all counts.  It's absolutely worth a serious try.

Unity, Unity…

You have to admit, talking about AC Unity isn’t easy: almost six years after the game’s disastrous release, the shadow of shame still hangs over Ubisoft and Unity.

Let’s get the elephant in the room out of the way straight away: YES, Unity still has bugs. Whether they relate to gameplay, optimisation or networking, Unity is still not quite up to scratch, even if it is now largely playable (thank goodness, after six years…).

But do we actually want to play it?

[h1] Story [/h1]

So let’s start with the story in the present day, and, er, well… There isn’t one, lol. You know, like in Black Flag when they made you pretend to be a video game tester and you had two or three cutscenes there? Well, no, you don’t get that anymore. They quickly throw in a bit of backstory just to justify the fact that… well, that Unity actually exists, and that’s it.

The story set in the past. That’s where I really struggle, actually. The basic plot seems fairly standard, really, but you could say the same about previous AC games. The main characters are quite likeable… Except perhaps Arno, who, in my opinion, has about as much charisma as a loaf of bread. Some sequences are truly forgettable – so much so that even after playing through the game for the third time, I felt as though I was discovering them for the first time – whilst others are absolutely sublime and make you want to keep playing. Do you see what I’m getting at? It feels as though Unity swings between the very mediocre and the very good, without ever striking a balance.

As for the side missions, they’re… well, they’re fine, but it’s a shame they’re so underutilised, really. For example, you can meet some very well-known characters who deserved a bit more (Madame Tussauds springs to mind, for instance) but who, in the end, are limited to a single line of dialogue and give you a run-of-the-mill mission along the lines of ‘kill the villain’ or ‘bring me that thing’ – and that’s a shame.

That said, there’s a co-op mode and, strangely enough, there are little storylines (or scenarios, if you like) and missions that are quite fun to play with other people; in fact, it really adds another dimension to the game and it’s interesting.

On the other hand, I was disappointed by the game’s ending, that’s all. I’m not going to give anything away, but I definitely felt that this ending was a massive middle finger from Ubisoft to all players, especially those who had the courage to see through to the end of a game that was unplayable at the time.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2122499056

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

In my opinion, Unity and Syndicate really did benefit from the best version of the Anvil engine. Paris is magnificent; the textures, lighting and shadow effects are at times breathtaking. The characters too (the main ones, that is – the NPCs are often rather ugly) have been given particular attention to detail, and they look truly superb.

The only downside is the NPCs, who really do look like potatoes, and the blood, which looks like ketchup. There’s clearly a gap in this area, and it’s always a bit odd to see.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1994053515

[h1] the RPG aspect [/h1]

Apparently, this is what people didn’t like about this game (well, amongst other things). Enemies have levels, you have a level, and you gain XP by killing enemies, helping the locals and completing missions. You earn skill points that make things a bit easier (sometimes). You have outfits (each with its own specific skin, which you see in the cutscenes – cool, isn’t it?) that provide various benefits such as health, strength, etc.

I thought the system was nice and it didn’t try to overcomplicate things, which leaves you room for a bit of optimisation (well, let’s be honest, I just wanted to pimp Arno out with the outfits) without it being too much of a faff.

[h1] But do we recommend it or not? [/h1]

Well, honestly… I’ve played it three times; the storyline’s a bit shaky but it’s enjoyable to play. There are loads of side missions, Paris is a stunning city (at least in the game, lol), and I even caught myself enjoying it on several occasions. Unity might not be a great game, and is actually a rather mediocre AC title. It’s certainly not the sort of game that’ll blow your mind or move you to tears. But given the price you can pick it up for (often €8 in the Steam sales), and bearing in mind that its only expansion, Dead Kings, is free, I reckon it’s a bit of fun that can keep you occupied for a few hours.

Anyone who is facing the "Account suspended" message on Ubisoft Connect, the fix is:
1. Completely close Ubisoft Connect from Task Manager / System Tray
2. Disable Wi-Fi / Unplug Ethernet
3. Launch Unity through Steam
4. If Ubisoft Connect asks for both Ubisoft email and password, enter them and check "Remember me"
5. Click "Play offline" and Unity will launch successfully
6. Then quit the game through main menu
7. Enable Wi-Fi / Plug Ethernet
8. Launch Unity and it'll run fine

But there's a problem. When I did this, I couldn't play AC Unity online/co-op. The game kept saying that we couldn't connect to Ubisoft servers, or a similar message like this.
